instruction: GUI-only requirement: Complete the task entirely in the launched Bonsai/Blender graphical user interface. Do not open Terminal or a shell; do not use the Blender Python console, Text editor scripts, Python, IfcOpenShell, shell commands, or any helper script/macro to directly generate or edit the deliverable file. Use only Bonsai/Blender native GUI tools, panels, menus, dialogs, and built-in save/export commands. Studio shell split into two spaces. The Desktop contains an editable IFC4 seed file at /home/user/Desktop/init.ifc. Open that seed project in Bonsai through the graphical IFC project open controls, inspect it as needed. The seed contains placeholder space names and no final window objects. Use the Bonsai/Blender GUI to rename the spaces to the required room names and add the required window objects, then save the only required deliverable on the Desktop as /home/user/Desktop/result.ifc using Bonsai's graphical IFC save/export controls. The saved IFC should contain a studio shell split into living and sleep spaces. Model the building as a rectangular single-storey shell about 7 m by 4 m with walls about 3.0 m high and one floor slab. Create real IfcSpace objects named Living, Sleep. Include at least 5 wall-like IfcWall or IfcWallStandardCase elements, at least 1 IfcSlab, at least 2 IfcDoor elements, and at least 2 IfcWindow elements. Create real IFC/BIM elements rather than ordinary Blender mesh placeholders or visual-only geometry. The exported IFC should use the IFC4 schema and have unique GlobalId values for IfcRoot objects. The shaped model should have an overall size roughly matching the shell, with X span about 7 m, Y span about 4 m, and Z span about 3.0 m. Other coordinates, wall thicknesses, opening positions, materials, object type names, relationship nesting, property sets, and harmless exporter metadata may vary as long as the saved IFC satisfies these requirements.
